children.text: tṛtīye garbhamāse 'raṇī āhṛtya ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā jayaprabhṛtibhir hutvā paścād agner darbheṣv āsīnāyāḥ patnyāḥ sarvān pramucya keśān navanītenābhyajya triśyetayā śalalyā śamīśākhayā ca sapalāśayā punaḥ patnīm agnir adāditi sīmantaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: In the third month of pregnancy, after bringing the fire-drill, or in the sixth or eighth month, he offers oblations with the formulas beginning with <s>Jaya</s>. Then, west of the fire, while his wife is seated on <s>darbha</s> grass, he loosens all her hair, anoints it with fresh butter, and, with a three-white-marked porcupine quill and a <s>śamī</s> branch together with <s>palāśa</s> leaves, he performs the <s>sīmanta</s> (parting of the hair), reciting, "Again <s>Agni</s> has given the wife."

children.text: aṣṭame garbhamāse jayaprabhṛtibhir hutvā phalaiḥ snāpayitvā yā oṣadhaya ity anuvākenāhatena vāsasā pracchādya gandhapuṣpair alaṃkṛtya phalāni kaṇṭhe vai saṃsṛjyāgniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In the eighth month of pregnancy, after offering with the formulas beginning with <s>Jaya</s>, he bathes her with fruits while reciting the section beginning "Yā oṣadhayaḥ"; he covers her with an unworn garment, adorns her with perfumes and flowers, fastens fruits around her neck, and has her circumambulate the fire clockwise.

children.text: prajāṃ me narya pāhīti mantreṇopasthānaṃ kṛtvā guṇavato brāhmaṇān bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: After making reverential attendance with the mantra, "Protect my offspring, O manly one," he should feed Brahmins of good qualities.
He should give fruits as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).
Then he should also perform the <s>svastyayana</s> (benediction for well-being).
He should honor the person who is his <s>guru</s> (teacher or elder).
